AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Image registration (IR) is an important process of developing a spatial relationship between pre-operative data and the physical patient in the operation theatre. Current IR techniques for Computer Assisted Orthopaedic Surgery (CAOS) are time consuming and costly. There is a need to automate and accelerate this process.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Bespoke quick, cost effective, contactless and automated 3D laser scanning techniques based on the DAVID Laserscanner method were designed. 10 cadaveric knee joints were intra-operatively laser scanned and were registered with the pre-operative MRI scans. The results are supported with a concurrent validity study.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The average absolute errors between scan models were systematically less than 1 mm. Errors on femoral surfaces were higher than tibial surfaces (P<0.05). Additionally, scans acquired through the large exposure produced higher errors than the smaller exposure (P<0.05).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: This study has provided proof of concept for a novel automated shape acquisition and registration technique for CAOS.
